lockFileMaintenance.description: Refresh the committed lockfiles on a schedule so transitive advisories get fixed. Renovate only proposes updates for the direct declarations it manages, so a vulnerable package that no manifest names is never reached by an ordinary update or by a vulnerability alert, and its advisory stays open until the lockfile is regenerated. The Friday early-morning window matches the maintainer's preference for scheduled dependency work, and automerge matches the non-major bundle policy: required status checks still gate the merge, so a refresh that breaks a check stays open for review.

customManagers.description: The commitlint versions pinned inline in the commitlint workflow and in scripts/commitlint-local. No built-in manager reads a version out of a shell script or a workflow run step, and the two must move together or a local check disagrees with CI.

packageRules.description: Bundle every non-major update into one automergeable pull request. Major updates are deliberately excluded so that a pending major never holds back the bundle.

prBodyNotes: Automation validates this dependency-only update and runs the ordered OpenRewrite and Spotless pipeline.
When an eligible non-major update produces no repository change, required CI passes and Renovate automerges this pull request.
When the toolchain changes source or POM output, this pull request remains blocked and automation opens or refreshes a separate generated pull request for maintainer review.
Major updates are created automatically and require manual merge through the repository-wide major-update guard.
Quarkus updater recipe changes MUST NOT be validated as general OpenRewrite maintenance updates.
Before merge, a maintainer MUST review the target Quarkus migration guide, run `quarkus:update` in the dependency-update branch, review the complete diff, and pass the full Maven gate.
After Renovate updates `tessl.json`, run `tessl install`, review the refreshed `.tessl/tiles` diff, and commit those vendored tile changes before merging.

packageRules.description: Major updates land one at a time and require a human merge after review of the migration notes. This rule deliberately sets no groupName: majors are already ungrouped because the bundle rule matches non-major types only, and forcing a groupName here would split lockstep groups whose members must move together across a major boundary.
